result.summary: D-79 is stably closed and the anchor-collapse attack failed on every assigned vector. BOTH suppression sides provably use the new signature because there is only ONE side that computes: continuityIssueSignature is defined once (continuity-flags.ts:53) and called once (toContinuityFlags:86); the scan route stores that value at flag creation (scan/route.ts:152) and tests membership against it (scan/route.ts:134 → continuity-flags.ts:87), while intentional/route.ts merely flips row status and never computes a signature — no second implementation exists to drift (grep-verified across src). The min(chapters) anchor is exactly the death chapter and is stable: graph-queries.ts:442 uses strict `>` vs c.deathChapter so every post-death chapter exceeds the anchor, and deathChapter itself is first-write-wins (coalesce, graph-builder.ts:270), clearable only by an authoritative edit (line 324) whose null-clear is mutually exclusive with the coalesce-stamp (deriveEntityGraphProps stamps only when isDeadStatus is true, the clear requires it false — no SET-order conflict in one query). False-suppression attacks: two simultaneous distinct dead_character_reappears for the same entity+anchor are structurally unrepresentable (one issue per Character node, single deathChapter property); die-ch4 → authoritative resurrection → die-ch20 yields anchor 20 → distinct signature → new flag (test-pinned); the only collision path (authoritative clear + re-death stamped at the SAME chapter) reproduces the exact contradiction the writer already declared intentional, so suppressing it matches intent. The disclosed residual is genuinely bounded to ONE re-surface per pre-fix intentional row: the new anchor signature is invariant thereafter, an undismissed re-surfaced flag persists as a single row (upsert update:{} + planFlagSync sees it active) rather than multiplying, pre-fix ACTIVE rows self-heal in one scan via toDelete, and stale old-format intentional rows are inert forever (their multi-chapter preimages can never be regenerated by the single-chapter scheme). All other flag types hash their full chapter set byte-identically to before (strict type check in signatureChapters; test-pinned for timeline_violation pairs). Non-blocking notes: second-death subsumption when the writer never authoritatively resurrects (pre-existing single-death-anchor model limit, deferred sub-fix (d)/task #46 — not introduced here, and the pre-fix "alert" for it was only the D-79 churn itself); GET-route flag descriptions freeze at first-detection evidence while the signature stays invariant; sub-fix (d) must preserve anchor stability when it lands or it will re-trigger a one-time re-surface wave.

findings.claim: Second death WITHOUT an authoritative resurrection is subsumed into the dismissed arc (no new flag) — pre-existing model limit, not introduced by this change; belongs to deferred sub-fix (d)
findings.detail: Path: character dies ch4, flag dismissed [Intentional] (sig anchored 4); writer never runs an authoritative correction, so the node stays status=dead with deathChapter=4 (coalesce first-write-wins, graph-builder.ts:270). A narrative second death at ch20 cannot be represented — the ch20 death event just joins postDeathChapters as more evidence of the SAME anchored-4 issue, so reappearances after ch20 stay suppressed. This is a miss, but it originates in the graph model (single sticky deathChapter — D-19 design, untouched here), not in the signature narrowing: even under the OLD full-chapter signature the emitted issue was still ONE issue, and the old re-fire carried zero specificity (it re-fired every chapter regardless of second deaths — the exact D-79 blocking churn). The authoritative-resurrection path DOES produce a distinct anchor-20 flag (test-pinned). Proper fix is sub-fix (d) (deathChapter = earliest death EVENT, task #46, explicitly deferred in the handoff).

findings.claim: Stored flag description/chapterNumber freeze at first-detection state now that the signature is invariant while the arc grows
findings.detail: scan/route.ts:152-167 upserts with update:{} — with the signature now stable, the SAME row persists as the reappearance list grows, so the stored description ('participates in chapters 6') and chapterNumber never refresh to include ch7, ch8, etc. The POST /scan response builds from freshly-detected flags (full current list), but GET /api/books/[id]/continuity returns the stale stored row — a mild POST/GET display inconsistency. Cosmetic evidence-staleness only; jump target (the death) and identity are unaffected. Pre-fix 'freshness' was the churn bug itself.

findings.claim: Residual re-surface is confirmed bounded to exactly once per pre-fix intentional flag; no unbounded re-fire path exists
findings.detail: Old intentional row S_old (full-chapter hash) fails to match the new anchor sig S_new once → one re-surfaced active flag; after re-dismissal S_new is stable forever (anchor = first-write-wins deathChapter; postDeath growth cannot move min because graph-queries.ts:442 enforces strictly-greater chapters). While undismissed, every scan recomputes the identical S_new → upsert no-op, single persistent row, not one per chapter. Pre-fix ACTIVE rows are replaced in one scan (S_old enters toDelete). Orphaned S_old intentional rows persist in DB and in the intentionalSignatures set but are inert: the new scheme emits only single-chapter preimages for this type, so an old multi-chapter signature can never be produced again — harmless cruft, could be swept in a later migration.

findings.claim: Other flag types keep full-chapter identity byte-identically — suppression is not weakened anywhere else
findings.detail: signatureChapters (continuity-flags.ts:38-44) narrows ONLY on the strict literal type match 'dead_character_reappears' (plus a correct chapters.length>0 guard preventing Math.min() → Infinity); every other type returns [...chapters], producing hash inputs identical to the pre-fix scheme. timeline_violation [earlier,later], location_conflict [chapter], relationship_contradiction [chapter]/[] remain chapter-sensitive (pinned by tests in both new suites). character_undocumented's growing list is irrelevant — dropped by toContinuityFlags before any signature is persisted.

findings.claim: Forward-compat warning for deferred sub-fix (d): changing deathChapter semantics will shift anchors and re-trigger a one-time intentional re-surface wave
findings.detail: The anchor equals whatever deathChapter the graph stamped (first-DETECTION chapter, not necessarily the narrative death event — e.g. a death first noticed while scanning ch7 anchors at 7). Stable today, but when sub-fix (d) (task #46) re-anchors deathChapter to the earliest death EVENT, existing dead nodes' anchors may move → anchor-signatures change → previously dismissed resurrection arcs re-surface once more. That dispatch should account for this (same one-time-bounded mechanics as this fix's disclosed residual) rather than discovering it as a regression.

result.summary: The attack's central question — does authoritative=true reopen RC-3 — resolves NO on the evidence: the autonomous window is real but NOT newly reachable. UpdateGraphEntity sits in 3 agent toolsets (Ghostwriter definitions.ts:59, Story Architect :125, World Researcher :366), executes with no approval gate (orchestrator.ts:853), and IS reachable unattended via the batch worker's coach→DelegateToSpecialist→full-toolset path (agent-worker.ts, tools.ts:1905-1955) — so a hallucinating overnight ghostwriter CAN authoritatively flip dead→alive. But at HEAD (the judged 3.0 baseline) this exact path already blanket-overwrote status/role/description via `ON MATCH SET n += $updateProps` with identical reachability and strictly MORE write power; D-80 restores pre-existing semantics on this one decision-level path (no prompt instructs routine graph writes — prompt-assembler injects graph context read-only) while the true RC-3 driver, per-scan extraction churn, stays sticky: repo-wide sweep confirms the ONLY production callers of upsertEntities are graph-maintenance.ts:295 (on-save scan) and :452 (rebuild), both default false, plus tools.ts:1544 (true); upsertSingleEntity is module-private; post-session has no direct call. The prior panel's own REJECT prescribed exactly this remedy ("make UpdateGraphEntity an authoritative write"), and the alternative (sticky tool reporting "1 updated" on a no-op) was itself a confirmed blocker. deathChapter=null is mutually exclusive with the RC-2 coalesce stamp (derive sets deathChapter only when isDeadStatus, graph-builder.ts:265-271 vs :312-325), leaves consistent state, and enables correct re-stamp of a later legit death — the non-clearing alternative would freeze a stale anchor forever. Injection boundary unchanged: authoritative values ride solely as $incoming* params (mergeParams :368-376), label via escapeLabelForQuery (:380), pinned by d80-1. Per the campaign rule the blocking bar is a NEW false flag or NEWLY-reachable stochastic corruption; neither is met — the corruption surface vs the judged product strictly shrank. The residual autonomous window deserves a cheap fast-follow guard (see finding 1) but is not a regression introduced by this bundle.

findings.claim: Autonomous authoritative window exists: unattended batch ghostwriter can hallucinate an UpdateGraphEntity call that flips dead->alive and erases deathChapter — real, but reachability and blast are <= the judged HEAD baseline, so non-blocking; guard recommended
findings.detail: Chain verified: agent-worker.ts runs writing-coach unattended; DelegateToSpecialist (tools.ts:1905-1955) spawns a full AgentOrchestrator with the specialist's complete toolset; Ghostwriter/Story Architect/World Researcher carry UpdateGraphEntity (definitions.ts:59/125/366); orchestrator.ts:853 executes it with no approval gate (APPROVAL_SENTINEL only wraps the separate RequestApproval tool). Post-D-80 such a call lands status/role/description directly and, for non-dead status, clears deathChapter. NOT blocking because (a) at HEAD the same path blanket-overwrote the same fields via `+= $updateProps` with identical autonomous reachability — RC-3 (D-32a) was driven by per-scan extraction churn, which remains sticky at both extraction call sites; (b) no system prompt instructs routine graph updates (prompt-assembler.ts's only graph section is read-only context injection at :1773), so invocation is decision-level and low-frequency, not per-chapter; (c) the field gate (isNonEmptyString) means an agent updating only description cannot touch status; (d) the prior panel's regression-blast REJECT explicitly prescribed this remedy, and the alternative (sticky tool lying '1 updated') was itself blocking. RECOMMENDED GUARD (fast-follow, cheap): 1) harden the tool description (tools.ts:566-569) to state it is an AUTHORITATIVE correction that overrides continuity protections and must only be used when the writer explicitly asks to correct the graph — never to record story events, which extraction captures automatically; 2) consider dropping UpdateGraphEntity from the ghostwriter toolset in unattended batch runs (or threading an interactive flag through ToolContext and downgrading authoritative to false when no user is present). Either closes the overnight window without reintroducing the D-80 lie in interactive sessions.

findings.claim: New-vs-HEAD primitive: authoritative un-death clears deathChapter, a property no caller could previously remove; abuse case is bounded and self-healing
findings.detail: Pre-fix, deathChapter was coalesce-first-write-wins against ALL writers; now graph-builder.ts:312-325 removes it on an authoritative Character non-dead status. Worst compound case: hallucinated authoritative un-death of a genuinely-dead character (autonomous window of finding 1), then a later scan re-asserts dead -> sticky adopts it and coalesce re-stamps deathChapter at the NEW chapter -> the D-79 anchor signature moves, so one previously-dismissed [Intentional] flag can re-fire ONCE with the new anchor and needs one re-dismissal (then stable — not a perpetual loop, and the flag reflects actual graph state at that time, so it is not a NEW false-flag class). The design is otherwise consistency-positive: without the clear, dead->alive would leave alive+stale-anchor and a later legitimate re-death could NEVER re-stamp (coalesce keeps the stale value). Clauses are mutually exclusive (derive stamps deathChapter only when isDeadStatus, :265-271), so no SET-ordering hazard; pinned by d80-1 (anchor retired, gate disarmed) and d80-3 (authoritative->dead still stamps).

findings.claim: Caller inventory verified: default authoritative=false everywhere except tools.ts:1544; extraction/rebuild/post-session stay sticky
findings.detail: Repo-wide grep (node_modules excluded): production callers of upsertEntities are exactly graph-maintenance.ts:295 (on-save scan path) and :452 (full rebuild) — both `upsertEntities(result)` with the default false — and tools.ts:1544 with explicit true. upsertSingleEntity is module-private (invoked only from upsertEntities' loop). post-session.ts never calls upsertEntities directly (routes through graph-maintenance); src/lib/graph/index.ts:4 is a re-export with no additional importers; no scripts/ or app-route callers exist. The wiring test (updategraphentity-authoritative.test.ts) pins executeTool('UpdateGraphEntity') -> upsertEntities(_, true) with bookId scoping intact (D-30).

findings.claim: Injection boundary (D-63) unchanged on authoritative writes: values param-only, label escaped; relationship-type cast remains guarded downstream
findings.detail: Authoritative branches emit `n.status = $incomingStatus` / `n.role = $incomingRole` / `n.description = $incomingDescription`; values enter only via mergeParams (graph-builder.ts:368-376), label via escapeLabelForQuery (:380); d80-1 asserts the value rides as a param and the sticky CASE text is absent. Residual (pre-existing, out of scope): executeUpdateGraphEntity still casts relationships[].type with no runtime allowlist (tools.ts:1533), but the operative guard is sanitizeRelationshipType at the Cypher boundary — untouched by this diff.

findings.claim: Non-canonical authoritative status ('Dead', ' dead ') stamps deathChapter without arming the gate — silent-miss residual, pre-existing family, unchanged
findings.detail: isDeadStatus trims+lowercases (so derive stamps the anchor and the null-clear is skipped) while the stored literal is written raw and the dead_character_reappears gate matches only the exact literal "dead". An authoritative 'Dead' therefore records an anchor but never arms the gate — a miss, not a false flag, in the same normalization family the sub-fix (b) panel already noted (its note 4) and the handoff defers to a future dispatch. No new exposure from D-80: the same asymmetry existed for stochastic writes pre- and post-(b).

result.summary: Both gates reproduce the executor's exact counts. STATIC RED: every new/extended test pins the real mechanism — genuinely RED pre-bundle are suppression-stability #1-2 (full-chapter hash breaks invariance/dismissal), the wiring test (1-arg call → authoritative undefined), monotonic b8/b9/d80-1 (label-blind sticky, missing 'mentioned' clause, no authoritative bypass), and the new continuity-flags invariance case; the rest (b8'/b9'/d80-2/d80-3, suppression #3/4/6) are correctly-designed anti-overreach and (b)-core-intact guards that would fail on the naive over-broad fixes, and none is a tautology or hardcoded-mock assert (the fake session discriminates on production query text; plain-assignment substrings verified non-overlapping with the CASE texts). The continuity-flags.test.ts chapter edit [12,19,20]→[11,18,20] was REQUIRED (old value collides with the default issue's anchor 12 post-fix), not test-gaming. DRIFT: sticky-dead CASE is byte-verbatim inside the Character-only branch; description CASE byte-identical; role CASE altered only by the sanctioned 'mentioned' empty-equivalent; RC-2 (chapter/occursInChapter-FP-A/deathChapter coalesce), D-27 alias union, RC-6 userId, D-63 escape, D-30 bookId binding all byte-intact; graph-maintenance/post-session/graph-queries untouched and both stochastic callers remain 1-arg (default false). (b)-CORE INTACT: d80-2/b1/b1' still pin sticky-dead for non-authoritative writes. Adversarial probes found no new false flag: deathChapter coalesce and =null clauses are provably mutually exclusive (complementary isDeadStatus guards on the same pristine properties.status); suppression write (scan upsert stores f.signature on bookId_signature) and read (intentionalSignatures) share the single continuityIssueSignature; Math.min anchor is always the death chapter; the agent tool input carries no aliases so authoritative edits cannot be swallowed by the alias early-return. Only note-level residuals remain.

findings.claim: Active dead_character_reappears DB row's description/chapters freeze at first detection while the arc grows (scan upsert update:{} no-op on stable signature); GET /continuity serves the stale evidence list while the scan response is fresh
findings.detail: src/app/api/books/[id]/continuity/scan/route.ts:152-166 upserts on bookId_signature with update:{}. Pre-D-79 each growth minted a new signature/row (the bug); post-fix the same row persists, so its stored description ('participates in chapters 6') lags the real list (6,7,8...). Cosmetic staleness of a TRUE flag, not a false flag; same pre-existing update-no-op pattern that already tolerated description-wording drift. Optional polish: refresh description/chapters in the upsert update branch.

findings.claim: Monotonic test's fake session would resolve a hypothetical coalesce + '= null' deathChapter co-occurrence in the OPPOSITE order to real Cypher (if/else-if picks coalesce; real SET last-item-wins picks null)
findings.detail: tests/unit/graph-entity-property-monotonic.test.ts:109-113. Unreachable today: the clauses are mutually exclusive by construction (coalesce iff isDeadStatus(properties.status), null iff authoritative && Character && !isDeadStatus(same value) — src/lib/graph/graph-builder.ts:265-271 vs 306-318, with deriveEntityGraphProps reading pristine properties before the allProps deletes). Cannot mask a current bug, only a future regression that makes them co-occur.

findings.claim: Authoritative dead-marking via UpdateGraphEntity without chapterNumber (tool defaults to 0) sets status='dead' but stamps no deathChapter, so the gate stays unarmed — silent under-detection, not a false flag
findings.detail: src/lib/agents/tools.ts:1536 chapterNumber ?? 0; deriveEntityGraphProps requires chapterNumber >= 1 (graph-builder.ts:651-657, D-19 chapter-0 story-bible rule). Pre-existing semantics unchanged by this bundle; an agent supplying the death chapter arms the gate correctly via the untouched coalesce.

findings.claim: Agent naming a character by a stored alias creates a parallel node under the alias name (tool input schema has no aliases field, so the alias-match path never runs for authoritative writes)
findings.detail: src/lib/agents/tools.ts:1523-1527 maps only name/label/properties. Double-edged but net-safe for this bundle: it also guarantees an authoritative edit can never be silently swallowed by the alias early-return refresh path (graph-builder.ts:130-151). The parallel-node miss is pre-existing and belongs to deferred sub-fix (c) (task #45).

findings.claim: Pre-fix [Intentional] rows carry old full-chapter signatures and will resurface once after this lands (must be re-dismissed once); pre-existing ACTIVE flags self-heal
